tools.name: search_datasets
tools.description:
Search the AQUAVIEW catalog — a comprehensive collection of 268K+ global oceanographic, atmospheric, and marine datasets from 15 sources (NOAA, NDBC, IOOS, WOD, CoastWatch, etc.), intended for scientific research, data analysis, and environmental monitoring.

This searches METADATA — which datasets

tools.name: get_item
tools.description:
Fetch a single AQUAVIEW dataset item with full details, properties, and download links (assets).

STAC items embed assets inline — each asset includes an href (download URL) and media type, so there is no need for a separate "files" call.

Args:
    collection: The collection ID the item belongs to

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description:
List all available AQUAVIEW data collections (sources).

Returns a summary of each collection with ID, title, description, spatial/temporal extent, and keywords. Use collection IDs to filter searches.

These are CATALOG collections. Several are also queryable row by row — see
list_data_sources for t

tools.name: aggregate
tools.description:
Run aggregation queries on the AQUAVIEW catalog — get counts, spatial distributions, temporal distributions, and per-collection breakdowns without fetching individual items.

Args:
    aggregations: Comma-separated aggregation types (required). Valid types: total_count, datetime_max, datetime_min, d

tools.name: list_data_sources
tools.description:
List the AQUAVIEW data sources you can pull actual rows from, or describe one in detail.

Call this BEFORE get_data on a source you have not used. Variable names are
canonical per source and cannot be guessed — this is where they come from.

With an API key, sources your account is entitled to appea

tools.name: get_data
tools.description:
Pull actual observation rows from an AQUAVIEW data source — not catalog metadata.

Use this whenever the question needs the measurements themselves (temperature
profiles, float positions, buoy readings), rather than which datasets exist.
Call list_data_sources first for a source's canonical variable
